title: Network operator safety norms & audit telemetry — PRD sketch
content:
Draft: Network Operator Safety Norms and Audit Telemetry — Private Deployments PRD (working notes)

Purpose
- Define a minimal, operator-focused set of controls and telemetry for customer-managed networking and the operator approval surface in Redwood Private.
- Ensure audit logs and approval gates provide adequate forensic capability, meet common enterprise compliance asks, and preserve customer privacy.
- Provide a practical rollout path that avoids large infra breakage and supports both self-service and SRE-assisted onboarding.

Background & motivation
- Customers deploying Redwood in VPC/on-prem consistently ask for: clear audit trails for network changes, operator approval flows for sensitive handoffs, and deterministic telemetry to troubleshoot handoffs.
- Current private-deploy feature set is fragmented: some events are logged, but schema is inconsistent; approvals are ad-hoc (email/Slack); operator roles are not well-scoped.
- Goal: create a repeatable, minimally invasive pattern that can be adopted across customers and integrated with KMS, SIEM and SIEM connectors.

Scope (this doc)
- Audience: product, infra, SRE, solutions engineering, and security reviewers.
- Feature areas: audit log schema + retention guidelines, approval gate primitives, operator role model and safe defaults, telemetry sampling and correlation IDs, handover runbooks.
- Out of scope: full SIEM integrations (connectors will be described in follow-up doc), billing telemetry, or agent-side network instrumentation beyond event emission.

User stories (examples)
- As a customer SOC analyst, I need reliable per-request audit events (who/what/when/where) for any operator-initiated network change so I can investigate incidents.
- As a platform operator at customer, I need a UI-driven approval gate for VPC peering or public egress enablement with an auditable approval record.
- As a Redwood SRE, I need telemetry that ties a customer approval to the deployment pipeline run (correlation id) so we can trace failures in rollouts.

Design constraints & principles
- Minimal surface: prefer a small, consistent event schema that covers most needs rather than many specialized event types.
- Privacy-first: redact customer data by default; provide opt-in fields for verbose logs retained under customer policy.
- Declarative approvals: approvals should be stored as structured artifacts with cryptographic signing of operator identity where possible (audit trail integrity).
- Forward-compatible: design event schema to allow adding fields rather than renaming.

Core requirements (MUST)
1) Audit log schema and events
   - Standard event fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, customer_id, deployment_id, operator_id (redacted if requested), action, resource, outcome, correlation_id, request_payload_hash, reason_text
   - Event examples: NETWORK_HANDOFF_REQUESTED, NETWORK_HANDOFF_APPROVED, NETWORK_HANDOFF_REJECTED, ROUTE_TABLE_UPDATE, FIREWALL_RULE_CHANGE, KMS_KEY_ACCESS
   - Retention default: 90 days in Redwood hosted control plane; option for customers to export to S3/GCS or SIEM with configurable retention up to customer policy
   - Integrity: events must be append-only; retention purge requires an auditable request (who requested purge, reason)
2) Approval gate primitives
   - Types: manual (human review), policy-driven (automated checks), delegated (customer-operator vs Redwood SRE)
   - Approval artifact: approval_id, approver_id, approver_role, timestamp, decision (approve/reject), justification, linked_event_ids, signed_blob (optional)
   - SLO: majority of manual approvals should be visible in the console and have decision latency < 4 hours for enterprise tier (configurable per-customer)
3) Operator role model and safe defaults
   - Roles: network-operator (customer), account-admin (customer), redwood-sre, redwood-platform-ops
   - Least-privilege: default operator token scopes exclude fatal operations (e.g., DNS takeover, KMS delete) unless explicitly enabled by account-admin with approval gate
   - Escalations: define auto-escalation path to account-admin or Redwood AE if approval times out or for high-risk actions
4) Telemetry & correlation
   - Correlation id strategy: generate correlation_id at user request entry point and propagate through orchestration, infra changes and approval artifacts
   - Sampling: capture full telemetry for approval flows; sample 1% of low-risk background network reconciliations with enriched payloads sent to internal observability for performance tuning
   - Telemetry fields: latency_ms, operator_latency_ms, orchestration_stage, infra_errors, retry_count
5) Onboarding and handover runbooks
   - Provide a checklist for customers and SEs: preflight network validation, key distribution (KMS/HSM), firewall rules baseline, test traffic plan, audit export configuration
   - Include a signed acceptance step where the customer acknowledges audit retention limits and approval gate behavior

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD)
- Audit queries: provide time-range, operator, action, resource filters with export to CSV/JSON within console
- Immutable snapshots: ability to snapshot approval artifacts and related logs for a timeframe (e.g., 30 days) for legal hold
- Performance: emitting audit events must add <10ms median latency to control-plane operations; approval gate lookups <50ms if cached
- Security: logs transit encrypted to customer SIEM endpoints; server-side encryption keys optional customer-managed

Operational flows (sketch)
- Flow A: Customer initiates network handoff (self-serve)
   1) System emits NETWORK_HANDOFF_REQUESTED with correlation_id
   2) Policy checks run (CIDR conflicts, reserved IPs, required tags)
   3a) If policy pass and customer policy auto-approve enabled -> emit APPROVED and apply changes
   3b) If manual review required -> create approval artifact and notify approvers (console + email + webhook)
   4) Approval decision stored, signed; changes execute with post-change verification events (ROUTE_TABLE_UPDATE, FIREWALL_RULE_CHANGE)
- Flow B: Redwood SRE-assisted onboarding (high-touch)
   1) SE creates a change ticket referencing JIRA id and handoff details in console
   2) Approval artifact created with delegated approver set to redwood-sre + account-admin oversight
   3) After completion, SE uploads signed PKI evidence and exports audit bundle for customer archive

Acceptance criteria (for 1.0)
- Console shows approval artifacts and linked events for 100% of operator-initiated network changes during QA runs
- Audit export to S3/GCS completes with manifest and checksum and is consumable by a sample SIEM (tested end-to-end)
- Triage run: correlation id traces from handoff request to infrastructure changes in at least 95% of test scenarios
- Security review signed off and threat model mitigations documented

Migration and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (internal pilot): implement schema and emit events in staging with Redwood-owned test customers (2 customers). Collect perf metrics and iterate.
- Phase 1 (early customers): opt-in export and console preview; SRE-assisted handovers only.
- Phase 2 (GA): enable self-serve approval flows with default constraints and retention policies; provide docs and runbook templates.

Open questions / risks
- Q1: Should approval artifacts be cryptographically signed by Redwood only, or provide option for customer-side signing (HSM)? (security team leaning: optional customer-side signing for regulated customers)
- Q2: How to model PII inside request_payload_hash vs storing full payload (tradeoff: forensic value vs privacy)?
- Q3: Retention SLAs — customers with legal hold needs will require much longer retention and potentially separate billing for storage.
- Risk: Alert fatigue for ops if too many approval events are surfaced; need rate-limiting or aggregation rules.

Next steps / immediate todo
- Product: prioritize event schema and minimal approval artifact shape (owner: Aisha) — deliver draft schema by 2025-11-21
- Infra: prototype append-only event store (S3-backed) and signed append logs (owner: Marco) — prototype by 2025-12-05
- SE/Security: draft customer onboarding checklist and legal hold options (owner: Priya) — initial draft by 2026-01-10

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: we are aiming for a small consistent schema and clear operator semantics rather than a fully featured audit platform on day 1.
- Please annotate the schema table below in comments with recommended additional fields or removal candidates.

(End of sketch)
